newsitem.title: CHINA: Tianjin still aims for third China stock exchange.
newsitem.headline: Tianjin still aims for third China stock exchange.

text.p: The northern Chinese port of Tianjin, which hopes to be the site of the country's third stock exchange, will step up efforts this year to develop its financial and insurance services, Mayor Zhang Lichang said.
"The emphasis of Tianjin's economic ambition is on helping the securities market to flourish," Zhang told a recent meeting of city officials, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.

Tianjin, which along with Beijing and Shanghai is administered directly by the central government, has long sought the right to open a third stock exchange to cement its role as the economic centre of northern China.
Beijing so far has not approved the plan, preferring to focus on the country's two existing stock exchanges in Shanghai and Shenzhen, across the border from Hong Kong.

Zhang said Tianjin officials would still redouble their efforts to build stock exchange networks and begin a pilot programme for a futures market. They will also develop Tianjin's wholesale markets, improve trade facilities and expand financial and insurance business companies regionally and nationwide.
Tianjin's service industries accounted for 40.5 percent of the city's gross domestic product in 1996, up 1.5 percentage points from the year before, Xinhua said.
